verdict.rationale: Grafana documents local dev setups for parts of its stack: Loki runs locally in single-binary mode on a local filesystem backend with logs sent via Alloy, Mimir runs in monolithic mode as one binary, and the as-code CLI is described as suitable for local development. File-based provisioning supports dashboards and data sources. However, no evidence describes spinning up the Grafana server itself locally (Docker or binary), nor an end-to-end local workflow for testing instrumentation together with dashboards. Missing for 10: documented local or Docker install of the Grafana server itself, an end-to-end local stack for instrumentation plus dashboard testing, independent or hands-on corroboration of a local dev setup.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up a local or dev instance of the platform to test instrumentation and dashboards

citations.quote: Try it locally. The fastest way to experiment is to run Loki in monolithic (single-binary) mode with a local filesystem backend and send logs to it with Grafana Alloy.
Use the monolithic mode to get up and running with just one binary and no added dependencies.
It’s suitable for CI/CD pipelines, local development
You can define data sources and dashboards using files that can be version controlled, making GitOps more natural.
or even locally on the filesystem
